answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The trellis multiplier is published, charged in marble, and pulse lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4036 identities would post 4381 proofs and burn roughly 60 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
